    Crowns in minimal representation-infinite algebras #

    Let A have a twisted multiplicative basis over P, and suppose every proper quotient of A is representation-finite. Then every closed chain (crown) of P contains a morphism factoring through any given non-invertible nonzero τ: otherwise the crown survives in P/τ, and A/⟨τ⟩ is representation-infinite (RayQuiver.MulBasis.crown_meets). This is the first step of the strategy of BO13a, Proposition 2 ("each long morphism τ occurs in C").
